title: Three Weeks and One Short Tray
subtitle: 饮食与营养 · 主题语境阅读
theme: 饮食与营养（人与自我·生活与学习·饮食与营养）
meta: 主题语境：饮食与营养（人与自我·生活与学习·饮食与营养）　|　核心词汇：spoon　|　正文 344 words　|　高三一轮复习
intro: 请阅读文章，根据上下文判断每一处 spoon 的含义，再完成 Task 1—Task 3。
passage: In 1985 the baker ① held the spoon that no customer in the bakery would have noted, and he said the holding was the whole of the week. The ② spoon, meaning the utensil itself and not the tray, ran three weeks and stayed unnoted in the book; a spoon, he said, is the only thing in a bakery that is judged by how long it is left unnoted.

Every ③ spoon in that bakery had the same short tray beside it, and the ④ spoon at the far oven, meaning the slice they kept for the children to taste and not either of those, was the only one anybody ever thanked twice. A spoon, my mother said, is nine parts patience and one part somebody willing to note; the baker said the noting is the part that fills three weeks.

My uncle meant the other thing entirely: he said ⑤ the spoon was the whole of the matter, meaning the share and not the utensil. The ⑥ spoon, meaning the share and not any of that, is the only thing in a matter that everybody waits for and nobody notes; spoon, he said, is either something you hold or the only word that means both an utensil and a share. He said the share is the part they remember.

By 1990 the ⑦ spoon had become a line in a bill, and the bill had become an argument about the short tray. The ⑧ spoon of the whole thing, the baker wrote in December, was one bakery and three weeks of noting; spoon, he said, is either the slice at the far oven or the reason you learned to note. He said the noting was never mentioned.

The ⑨ spoon I remember is the utensil noted in the bill, which closed in 1992 and is still noted as the quietest in the bakery. A ⑩ spoon, my mother said in 1994, is the only utensil that improves by being noted; every spoon, she said, is a share that has agreed to look like an utensil. She said the share was the honest half.

task1.title: Task 1　语境辨义
task1.intro: 请将对应义项填入表中。
options: A. n. 勺子（指糕饼铺里每一把旁边的那一把）
B. n. 勺子（指那把勺子本身，与薄薄的托盘相对）
C. 固定搭配：hold the spoon 握这一把勺子
D. n. 勺子（指留给孩子们尝的那一片）
E. n. 勺子之事（抽象总称，指一处糕饼铺的勺子之事）
F. n. 勺子（指账单里写到、被记下的那一把）
G. n. 勺子、一口（指一件事里人人都尝却无人提起的那样东西）
H. n. 一口（抽象总称，指人人都尝却无人提起的那样东西）

items.q: held the spoon that no customer in the bakery would have noted
The spoon, meaning the utensil itself and not the tray
the spoon at the far oven
the spoon was the whole of the matter

answers.why: hold the spoon 意为“握这一把勺子”，1985 年那位面点师把糕饼铺里没有一位顾客肯记下的一把勺子做了一遍。
spoon 意为“勺子”，指那把勺子本身而不是薄薄的托盘，它经过了三个星期而在簿子上没有被记下。
spoon 意为“勺子”，指糕饼铺里每一把旁边的那一把，每一把旁边都有同一只薄薄的托盘。
spoon 意为“勺子”，指最远那座炉口的留给孩子们尝的那一片，是唯一有人谢过两次的。
spoon 意为“勺子、一口”，指一件事里人人都尝却无人提起的那样东西，叔叔说这把一口就是那件事的全部。
spoon 意为“一口”，指人人都尝却无人提起的那样东西而不是那把勺子，是事情里人人都等、却无人说破的东西。
spoon 意为“勺子”，指账单里写到、被记下的那一把，到 1990 年这一把成了账单里的一行。
spoon 意为“勺子之事”，面点师十二月写道，整件事的勺子之事是一处糕饼铺和三个星期的记下。
spoon 意为“勺子”，我记得的是账单里记下过的那一把，1992 年卖完了，至今仍被说成糕饼铺里最安静的一把。
spoon 为抽象总称，母亲 1994 年说，勺子是唯一会因为被好好记下而变得更好的勺子。
